title: The Respiratory System
hook: With every breath, your lungs trade carbon dioxide for fresh oxygen — the gas swap that keeps every cell in your body running.
key_points: The respiratory system brings in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide.
Air travels down the windpipe into the lungs' branching airways.
Gas exchange happens in tiny air sacs called alveoli.
Oxygen passes into the blood while carbon dioxide passes out to be exhaled.
content_html: Breathing is so automatic you rarely notice it, but each breath drives one of the body's most vital trades. The respiratory system pulls in air, extracts the oxygen your cells need to release energy, and gets rid of carbon dioxide, the waste gas they produce. Without this constant exchange, cells would suffocate within minutes.
extra_html: Air enters through your nose and mouth, flows down the windpipe (trachea), and branches into ever-smaller tubes inside the lungs, ending at millions of tiny air sacs called alveoli. Their walls are extraordinarily thin and wrapped in blood vessels, so oxygen slips easily into the bloodstream while carbon dioxide passes out to be exhaled. The diaphragm, a dome of muscle beneath the lungs, drives the bellows action: it flattens to pull air in and relaxes to push it out. As NIH MedlinePlus describes, this teamwork between airways, alveoli, and muscle keeps oxygen flowing to every corner of the body.

related.title: The Circulatory System
related.hook: Your heart pumps blood through roughly 60,000 miles of vessels, delivering oxygen and fuel to every cell and hauling waste away — about once a minute.

related.title: Cellular Respiration
related.hook: Every cell in your body slowly 'burns' sugar with oxygen to release energy — the same chemistry as photosynthesis, run in reverse.

flashcards.prompt: What is the main job of the respiratory system?
flashcards.back_html: To bring oxygen into the body and carry carbon dioxide out — the gas exchange that supplies cells with the oxygen they need and clears their waste gas.

flashcards.prompt: Where in the lungs does gas exchange actually happen?

choices.text: In tiny air sacs called alveoli

flashcards.explanation_html: The lungs end in millions of microscopic sacs called alveoli, whose thin walls sit right against blood vessels — the perfect place for oxygen and carbon dioxide to swap.

flashcards.prompt: What does the blood pick up at the alveoli?

choices.text: Oxygen, while releasing carbon dioxide to be exhaled
Neither — the blood just passes through

flashcards.explanation_html: At the alveoli, oxygen crosses into the blood and carbon dioxide crosses out, so blood leaves the lungs oxygen-rich and you breathe the carbon dioxide away.
